title.narrative: Catalysing Access to Pit Latrine Emptying Equipment in East Africa

description.narrative: OPERO Services Ltd will catalyse access to pit latrine emptying equipment in East Africa via (i) purchasing a range of equipment and providing training on its use; and (ii) establishing a supply chain for one exemplary piece of equipment, the PuPu pump. By catalysing access to pit latrine emptying equipment, we anticipate playing a key role in the development of the onsite sanitation service delivery market in Kenya and beyond.

title.narrative: 6.3- Current stage of innovation

description.narrative: Select current stage of your innovation/initiative

actual.value: We are currently at the proof-of-concept stage, where we aim to successfully implement pilot programs that will validate the effectiveness of the PuPu pump. These initiatives are designed to gather valuable data and user feedback, allowing us to refine our approach based on real-world experiences. Additionally, we are compiling a report detailing potential market routes for the PuPu pump, based on data collected from 25 counties across Kenya. This report considers the existing market and the enabling environment in each surveyed county, providing further insights for our strategies. By successfully implementing these pilot programs and leveraging the insights from our county reports, we hope to build a strong case for transitioning to scale. This will enable us to expand our efforts and ensure that the benefits of the PuPu pump reach more communities, contributing to sustainable sanitation practices.

title.narrative: 1- Improved access to safe water, sanitation and IWRM services/products
S1- Total number of current unique users served by the initiative with access to improved and safe sanitation products and services

description.narrative: Fill in total number of unique current users for sanitation. Disaggregated per: Male/Female. Type: Domestic users (private and households), school users and for other public users (e.g markets and hospitals, communal users etc) Finally disaggregate users that are provided with a Safely managed / Basic service / Limited service from the initiative. The initiative must tick all criteria to be considered as that service level. 1) Safely managed service: - the initiative provides an improved sanitation facility (this includes: flush/pour flush to piped sewer system, septic tanks or pit latrines; ventilated improved pit latrines, composting toilets or pit latrines with slabs) - the initiative's sanitation service is not shared with other households - the initiative ensures that human excreta are safely disposed in situ or transported and treated off-site 2) Basic service: - the initiative provides an improved sanitation facility (this includes: flush/pour flush to piped sewer system, septic tanks or pit latrines; ventilated improved pit latrines, composting toilets or pit latrines with slabs) - the initiative's sanitation facility is not shared with other households - initiative does not ensure that human excreta and urine is safely disposed / transported / treated 3) Limited service: Usually at baseline level, but cannot be included at target level. This includes, open pits, unimproved pit latrines, unlined pits, no slabs, prone to flooding etc \* This is indicative of the reach and scale of the initiative in reaching new users with its products and services in terms of the service level that is being provided (as defined by JMP).
